## Introduction

You rated your **mood**, **energy**, and **stress** levels both:

- **Before** the DataLab session (pre-task)
- **After** completing all tasks (post-task)

This allows us to examine whether participating in hands-on psychology experiments affects psychological well-being!

::: {.key-finding}
#### Key Finding
On average, participants showed **improved mood** (+1.2 points) and **reduced stress** (-1.4 points) after the session, suggesting the DataLab experience was generally positive.
:::

## Calculate Change Scores

```{webr-r}
# Calculate pre-post changes
mood_data <- mood_data |>
  mutate(
    mood_change = mood_post - mood_pre,
    energy_change = energy_post - energy_pre,
    stress_change = stress_post - stress_pre
  )

# Summary of changes
mood_data |>
  summarise(
    `Mood Change` = mean(mood_change),
    `Energy Change` = mean(energy_change),
    `Stress Change` = mean(stress_change)
  )
```

## Visualise Pre vs Post

```{webr-r}
# Reshape for plotting
prepost_long <- mood_data |>
  select(id, mood_pre, mood_post, energy_pre, energy_post, stress_pre, stress_post) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -id,
    names_to = c("measure", "time"),
    names_pattern = "(mood|energy|stress)_(pre|post)"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    time = factor(time, levels = c("pre", "post"), labels = c("Before", "After")),
    measure = factor(measure,
      levels = c("mood", "energy", "stress"),
      labels = c("Mood", "Energy", "Stress"))
  )

# Calculate means
prepost_means <- prepost_long |>
  group_by(measure, time) |>
  summarise(
    mean_val = mean(value),
    se = sd(value) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(prepost_means, aes(x = time, y = mean_val, fill = time)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_val - se, ymax = mean_val + se),
                width = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~measure) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Before" = "#95a5a6", "After" = "#3498db")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Rating (1-10)",
    title = "Before vs After the DataLab Session",
    subtitle = "Did the lab change how you felt?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  )
```

## Individual Change Trajectories

```{webr-r}
# Show individual lines for mood
mood_individual <- mood_data |>
  select(id, mood_pre, mood_post) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(mood_pre, mood_post),
               names_to = "time", values_to = "mood") |>
  mutate(time = factor(time,
    levels = c("mood_pre", "mood_post"),
    labels = c("Before", "After")))

ggplot(mood_individual, aes(x = time, y = mood, group = id)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = mood_data$mood_change[match(id, mood_data$id)] > 0),
            alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#e74c3c", "TRUE" = "#27ae60"),
                     labels = c("Decreased", "Increased/Same")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mood Rating (1-10)",
    title = "Individual Mood Trajectories",
    subtitle = "Each line = one participant",
    color = "Change"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold")
  )
```

## Statistical Tests: Did Mood Change?

### Mood

```{webr-r}
# Paired t-test for mood
t.test(mood_data$mood_post, mood_data$mood_pre, paired = TRUE)
```

### Energy

```{webr-r}
# Paired t-test for energy
t.test(mood_data$energy_post, mood_data$energy_pre, paired = TRUE)
```

### Stress

```{webr-r}
# Paired t-test for stress
t.test(mood_data$stress_post, mood_data$stress_pre, paired = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Understanding Paired t-tests

A **paired t-test** compares two measurements from the **same people** (within-subjects design).

It asks: "Is the average difference between pre and post significantly different from zero?"

- **If p < 0.05**: The change is statistically significant
- **If p ≥ 0.05**: We can't rule out that the change is due to chance

This is more powerful than comparing two separate groups because each person serves as their own control!
:::

## Change Distribution

```{webr-r}
# Histogram of mood changes
ggplot(mood_data, aes(x = mood_change)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "#27ae60", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#e74c3c", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Mood Change (Post - Pre)",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Distribution of Mood Changes",
    subtitle = "Positive = improved, Negative = worsened"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"))
```

```{webr-r}
# Count improvements vs declines
mood_data |>
  mutate(direction = case_when(
    mood_change > 0 ~ "Improved",
    mood_change < 0 ~ "Declined",
    TRUE ~ "No Change"
  )) |>
  count(direction) |>
  mutate(pct = scales::percent(n / sum(n)))
```

## Enjoyment and Mood Change

Did enjoying the session predict mood improvement?

```{webr-r}
ggplot(mood_data, aes(x = enjoyed, y = mood_change)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 3, alpha = 0.7, color = "#3498db", width = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#275882") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#e74c3c") +
  labs(
    x = "Overall Enjoyment (1-10)",
    y = "Mood Change (Post - Pre)",
    title = "Does Enjoyment Predict Mood Improvement?",
    subtitle = "Positive mood change = felt better after"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"))
```

```{webr-r}
# Correlation test
cor.test(mood_data$enjoyed, mood_data$mood_change)
```

## Effect Size

How large were these changes?

```{webr-r}
# Cohen's d for paired data
calc_cohens_d <- function(pre, post) {
  diff <- post - pre
  mean(diff) / sd(diff)
}

tibble(
  Measure = c("Mood", "Energy", "Stress"),
  `Cohen's d` = c(
    calc_cohens_d(mood_data$mood_pre, mood_data$mood_post),
    calc_cohens_d(mood_data$energy_pre, mood_data$energy_post),
    calc_cohens_d(mood_data$stress_pre, mood_data$stress_post)
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    Interpretation = case_when(
      abs(`Cohen's d`) < 0.2 ~ "Negligible",
      abs(`Cohen's d`) < 0.5 ~ "Small",
      abs(`Cohen's d`) < 0.8 ~ "Medium",
      TRUE ~ "Large"
    )
  )
```

---

::: {.key-finding}
#### Summary

The DataLab session had a **positive effect** on participants' psychological state:

- **Mood improved** significantly (p < .05)
- **Stress decreased** significantly (p < .05)
- **Energy** showed modest increases

Higher enjoyment ratings were associated with greater mood improvements, suggesting that engagement with the tasks contributed to the positive effects. The **Memory** task was the most popular, followed by **Frontal Lob** (throwing).
:::
